title: The Small Model Infrastructure Nobody Built (So We Did) — Filip Makraduli, Superlinked
talk_summary: Filip Makraduli describes Superlinked's open-source inference engine for small models (embeddings, rerankers, NER) used in AI search and document processing, covering hot-swapping models on shared GPUs, re-implementing forward passes for heterogeneous architectures, and Kubernetes autoscaling. The core argument is that small models should preprocess/filter context before it reaches agents, and that GPU utilization comes from multiplexing many small models rather than provisioning one GPU per model.

takeaways.technique: Small-model preprocessing to shrink agent context
takeaways.what_they_do: Run small specialized models (NER, classifiers, rerankers) as tools that filter/classify/retrieve data before it enters the main agent's context, to counter context rot.
takeaways.evidence_quote: using small models that can preprocess your data so that then you can actually use your agents

takeaways.technique: Hot-swap small models on shared capacity with LRU eviction
takeaways.what_they_do: Multiplex many small models onto one GPU with least-recently-used eviction instead of dedicating a GPU per model, raising utilization.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have this least recently used eviction policy that we've built in
takeaways.numbers: small models occupy 'a few gigabytes of memory' each

takeaways.what_they_do: Use Prometheus metrics with KEDA autoscaling and queuing to scale GPU pools and avoid idle hardware.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're doing KEDA auto scaling with Prometheus metrics in order to be able to kind of switch models around

takeaways.technique: Narrow task-specific models beat general APIs on tight tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: Route narrow, well-defined subtasks (classification, extraction, reranking) to small open models that match or beat managed services on those benchmarks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for very narrow tasks, open source models are beating managed services
